newsitem.title: USA: ICG sees improved revenue-cost relations.
newsitem.headline: ICG sees improved revenue-cost relations.

text.p: ICG Communications Inc said Tuesday that as higher-margin local telephone services are carried on ICG networks, the relationship between revenue and operating costs and selling, general and administrative expenses is expected to improve.
ICG today reported a net loss for second quarter of $77.6 million, compared with a loss of $64.7 million a year earlier. Loss per share was $2.42, compared with $2.43.
"We are pleased about our success in selling competitive local dial tone services," said Chief Executive Shelby Bryan.

"Clearly there is a pent-up demand for the competitive services offered by ICG, and we must now focus on provisioning these services to our customers. To facilitate and improve the provisioning process, we have launched several internal initiatives to automate our service delivery. This is only part of the provisioning challenge. As with all telephone competitors entering the local market place, we require the cooperation of Incumbent Local Exchange Carriers as prescribed by the 1996 Telecommunications Act and our interconnection agreements. For the most part, their current efforts to be cooperative can be characterized as slow and arduous."
